7. Oecus (4), E-wall. The central aedicule with a yellow background with the ceiling rendered in perspective enclosed a medallion with a female bust between two cupids (removed). The stucco moulded cornice above the upper red area with three aedicules encloses the yellow lunette of the fictitious vault.  77 N36057

8. Oecus (4), wall E, detail: the central medallion depicting the bust of Venus Genetrix with collar and jeweled diadem between two cupids. The curly hair fashionable in the Flavian era makes one suspect that it is rather the lady of the house portrayed in the guise of the goddess.  71 de Vos 31.19
9. Oecus (4), wall E, side panel N: painting on a red background with a kneeling cupid in the act of shooting an arrow at the rampant deer: an allusion to Diana the huntress.   7°7 N36069
10. Oecus (4), wall E, side panel S: painting on a red background with a pair of peacocks, sacred to Juno.  77 N36070

11. Oecus(4), E face, section N. The tripartition of the upper area with three aedicules reflects the façade with three doors with the respective avant-corps of the classical stage, to which the tragic female mask that crowns the volute tympanum of the side aedicules refers. The gaze of the mask turns to the center of the wall.  77 N36064

12. Oecus (4), E wall, upper area, central section. The feline (lion or panther) in the leafy aedicule with the shell-shaped basin and the two pavoniailatos of it, are animals that appear in the procession celebrating the triumph of Dionysus in the East. The peacocks and the clypeus hanging in the center of the coffered ceiling, painted at the end above the red background layer, and the architectural motifs also painted when the plaster was already too dry to form the colors applied in the third layer, are therefore becoming transparent.  77 N36063

13. Oecus(4), E wall, S section. The painter's particular care in rendering the ribbons results from the way he turns the corner in the panel of the middle area, as well as from the ribbon hanging behind the aedicule.  77 N36062

14. Oecus (4), S. Wall Side wall that echoes the decorative scheme of the opposite wall, without taking into account the openings of the two windows. The central medallion was damaged by the hole drilled by ancient explorers, who crossed the room obliquely (see fig. 1).  77 N36059
15. Oecus (4), S wall, middle area, detail: the central medallion, of which only the lower section remains, depicting part of a bust - portrayed with the left hand (right for the viewer).  77 N36071
16. Oecus (4), wall S, middle area, side panel O: painting on a red background with Dionysus as a child riding a panther behind with a bunch of grapes in his hand.  77 N36072

17. Oecus (4), S wall, upper red area with the interrupted design at the window. Of the candelabrum there is only the terminal volute supporting a box with a mask: a Dionysian allusion, like the tambourine hanging from the arched garland. 18. Oecus (4), S. The white shear of the splayed window, reflecting the light picked up from above, is decorated with a swan.  '77 N36065

21. Oecus(4), wall O, middle area, side panel N: painting with a red background with a cupid watering an animal.   77 N36074

1. The façade of the caupona has a painted female head, with her head covered by an elephant's body and ears of wheat, according to the scheme of the personification of Alexandria or Africa. The Mercury that appears next to it indicates the profit that was made with the trade of grain from Egypt. Under the sign we read the electoral manifesto C Gavium Rufum II vir of. The insignia was a pendant to that of the caupona I 12,3 - with the personification of Rome. A similar pair of busts personified by Alexandria and Sicily - which disappeared before being documented, was reported on one of the S-facades of the Via di Nola in the second quarter of the 19th century.  Spinazzola II, p. 156, fig. 193

The bed area is devoid of ornamentation.  77 N36633

The vast garden, common with the adjoining house I 15.1, has revealed the existence of a rich vegetable garden-orchard-vineyard; in the upper area old vines and trees were planted randomly arranged; in the lower area there were mainly vines, planted at regular intervals; In addition, vegetables and limes were grown in two well-defined areas.  Recent reconnaissance has revealed 416 root holes and along the perimeter walls, 28 ceramic pots with four holes in the bottom for the cultivation of exotic plants or for the reproduction of seeds and cuttings. In the corner S-É is a stable divided into QUARTO small rooms. The numerous anores found between the house and the garden suggest the marketing of agricultural products. The house, built during the second century as a peristyle stately quarter to enlarge the nearby house I 15,1, received its current layout in the middle of the first century BC: it was deprived of the portico E of the triclinium and the rooms, profoundly modified, were decorated in the second style. Repairs and changes were underway at the time of the eruption.
